title: Governance and sustainability of wakaf assets in Singapore
asked: Dr Hamid Razak asked what governance and oversight mechanisms ensure wakaf assets are managed according to donors' intentions while remaining financially sustainable, and how wakaf management has evolved to handle fragmented assets, rising maintenance costs and redevelopment constraints in land-scarce Singapore.
answered_by: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
response: The Acting Minister said all wakaf assets are vested in MUIS under AMLA and managed by Warees Investments and appointed mutawallis. He listed governance steps: MUIS Council approval of mutawallis, AMLA audit requirements and MUIS checks on Fatwa Committee guidance, and a MUIS Wakaf Disbursement Committee reviewing annual disbursements. He said rising costs and development needs make management harder, with MUIS and Warees keeping rents affordable while seeking returns, and using the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme for projects such as The Red House and Jamae Chulia Heritage Development. In 2024, $11.3 million was disbursed to beneficiaries including family members, mosques, madrasahs, community organisations and charities.

key_points.point: Ownership of all wakaf assets is vested in MUIS under AMLA.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: under the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA), the ownership of all wakaf assets is vested in the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, or Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS).

key_points.point: Wakaf assets are managed by Warees Investments, a MUIS subsidiary, and appointed mutawallis according to the donor's intentions.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: The wakaf assets are managed by Warees Investments, a subsidiary of MUIS, and the appointed mutawallis, in accordance with the intentions of the wakif or donor.

key_points.point: Mutawallis must be approved by the MUIS Council and have governance and sustainability competencies.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: all mutawallis must be approved by the MUIS Council and have the competencies to maintain good governance and long-term sustainability of the wakaf they oversee.

key_points.point: Warees and mutawallis must meet AMLA audit requirements and undergo MUIS checks on Fatwa Committee religious guidance.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Warees and the appointed mutawallis must comply with audit requirements set out under the AMLA, as well as undergo periodic checks by MUIS that religious guidance by the Fatwa Committee has been adhered to.

key_points.point: The MUIS Wakaf Disbursement Committee reviews annual disbursements and recommends allocations per the wakif's intention.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: the MUIS Wakaf Disbursement Committee, which comprises members from the MUIS Council, monitors and reviews annual wakaf disbursements, and makes recommendations on the allocation of wakaf funds, in accordance with the wakif’s intention.

key_points.point: MUIS and Warees keep rents affordable while seeking sufficient financial returns for beneficiaries.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Amidst rising costs and development needs, MUIS and Warees strive to keep rents affordable, while performing their fiduciary duty to ensure sufficient financial returns for the wakaf beneficiaries.

key_points.point: Asset enhancement and redevelopment are done under the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: MUIS and Warees have also undertaken asset enhancement and redevelopment initiatives under the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme to optimise financial returns while sustaining their heritage value.

key_points.point: Recent examples are The Red House at East Coast Road and Jamae Chulia Heritage Development at Mosque Street.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Recent examples include The Red House at East Coast Road and Jamae Chulia Heritage Development at Mosque Street.

key_points.point: In 2024, $11.3 million was disbursed to wakaf beneficiaries including family members, mosques, madrasahs, community organisations and charities.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: In 2024, a total of $11.3 million was disbursed to the wakaf beneficiaries, which include the family members of the benefactors, as well as mosques, madrasah, community organisations and charities.

key_points.point: Returns may be used to build and maintain mosques and madrasahs, support the poor and needy, and fund community development and welfare, depending on the wakif's intention.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Depending on the intention of the wakif, these returns may be used to build and maintain mosques and madrasahs, support the poor and needy, and also, fund the development and welfare of the community.

key_points.point: Engagement with Indian/Muslim community leaders included many sessions and clarifications on planning constraints.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: We tried to reach out to the Indian/Muslim community leaders, had many sessions, even went back and forth when they needed clarity, there were clarifications or even certain things that did not meet the planning criteria.

key_points.point: The Jamae Chulia Mosque restoration is completed and Jamae Chulia Heritage is to be completed soon.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: the Jamae Chulia Mosque restoration has been completed and the Jamae Chulia Heritage is going to be completed soon.

key_points.point: The minister said MUIS will do its best to ensure the wakif's wishes are acceded to and held with trust.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: we will do our best to ensure that what the wakif would like to leave behind is not only acceded to, but we hold it with trust.
